title: Choose the visual world
question: The owner rejected the rolled Certification Lab Workbook and pinned Apple's public product language: a quiet, product-led editorial system.

options.label: Quiet Systems
options.lineage: Apple public product pages and the category-default clean engineering portfolio, executed with restraint
options.thesis: The portfolio as a quiet, well-made product page: the interface recedes so the name, evidence, and one next action lead.
options.viewport: A frosted header, a left-aligned name hero with one blue action, a single-column selected-work sequence, and soft gray proof cards.
options.risk: Can read as generic if the case-study evidence and bilingual craft are not strong enough to carry the restraint.

raised.raise: A single at-a-glance status band reads all four certifications and seven case studies as one instrument row.
Completion, in-progress, and pending states are encoded in pattern and label as well as color, so they survive grayscale.
Each section commits to one dominant idea in hard asymmetry, never a symmetrical card grid.
Lab steps are discrete, deep-linkable states, each recoverable and replayable.
Objective codes and headlines are structural typography, not decoration.

options.label: Network Operations Runbook
options.lineage: network operations runbooks, shift handover binders, and change-control packs
options.thesis: The portfolio as an operations runbook: role, systems, and procedures documented for handover.
options.viewport: A tabbed binder page with a role summary, a system inventory, and procedure cards indexed down the page.
options.risk: Familiar operations documentation; may read as an internal runbook rather than a personal portfolio.

options.label: Metro Typographic Map
options.lineage: metro screen systems and network topology maps
options.thesis: The portfolio as a metro map of domains and case studies, each stop a proof point.
options.viewport: A panoramic line with stops for certifications and case studies, giant cropped lowercase type leading the pan.
options.risk: Bold and legible, but the color-field system can overpower technical detail.
options.case: Fuses well: network topology and metro maps share nodes, lines, and interchange logic, so audience identification is strong; clarity for a time-pressed recruiter is slightly lower.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.lineage: analog recording desks and broadcast metering
options.thesis: A row of measured instruments that reads the whole system at a glance.
options.viewport: A full-width bridge of identical meters, needles leaning in unison, channel labels beneath.
options.risk: Audio metering is not the audience's world; the metaphor would costume the portfolio.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a recording desk does not identify a network and security engineer, even though the measured-state idea is useful.

options.label: One-Bit Desktop
options.thesis: Case studies as overlapping windows on a single desktop plane.
options.viewport: Overlapping windows with title bars, dithered gray fills, and marching-ants selection.
options.risk: Nostalgia for early desktop UI does not identify a network and security engineer.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the desktop metaphor is legible but unrelated to the audience's professional world.

options.label: Cut-Paper Title Sequence
options.thesis: The portfolio as a timed sequence of cut-paper cards, one idea per card.
options.viewport: Full-bleed color fields with black silhouettes, skinny caps set off baseline, one idea per card.
options.risk: A cinematic sequence delays the recruiter's scan and can feel like style over proof.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the title-sequence rhythm is memorable but fights the fast, factual scan recruiters need.
options.kept: One dominant idea per section with hard asymmetry.

options.label: Origami Fold Sequence
options.thesis: A single sheet folded through deliberate steps into a finished form.
options.viewport: A centered square with numbered folds in the margin, crease pattern paired with a spatial view.
options.risk: The craft is beautiful but the folding metaphor has no professional relevance here.
options.case: Fuses poorly: paper folding does not identify a network and security engineer and adds a learning curve before the proof.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Letters become weather and reshape the landscape according to grammar.
options.viewport: A monumental grotesk breaking into rain and carving words across an open field.
options.risk: The transformation obscures the reading order and turns proof into spectacle.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience needs credentials and case studies, not a language experiment.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A portrait and headline hero followed by a row of equal project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
